newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi oil exports to follow U.N. distribution deal. [CORRECTED 13:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Iraqi oil exports to follow U.N. distribution deal. [CORRECTED 13:15 GMT]

text.p: Iraqi oil minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said on Wednesday (corrects from Monday) that his county would resume crude exports under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations as soon as a food distribution plan was completed.

"Iraq will resume oil exports under the oil-for-food and medicine agreement immediately after completing the distribution plan which is being discussed with the United Nations," Rasheed said, quoted by the official Iraqi News Agency (INA).

INA said Rasheed was commenting on reports which said Iraq had suspended its oil exports under the deal, which allowed Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil between last December and June to raise money to buy food and medicine for Iraqis, hit by U.N. sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The U.N. Security Council last week extended the programme for six more months. Baghdad has to submit to the U.N. a distribution plan before Iraq can start oil exports for the second six months.
The agency said it had learnt that Iraq's oil ministry was "holding meetings with international companies' representatives to export oil after concluding deals with them."
Iraq's U.N. co-ordinator Staffan de Mistura said earlier this month that Baghdad had not yet completed its distribution plan which would cover the central and southern parts of Iraq.
Distribution for the Kurdish north, out of control of the Iraqi government since 1991, would be prepared by the U.N.
Senior Iraq officials have frequently complained about the delay in implementing the distribution plan for the first six months.
Iraqi official media said on Wednesday that Iraq had asked the U.N. to allow Baghdad to use an Iraqi-Syrian land line, closed since the 1980s, to handle its purchases under the deal.
Iraq's purchases of food and medicine are now handled by its Um Qasr port in the Gulf, Jordan's Aqba port and via Turkish ports.
Iraqi and Syrian officials said earlier this month they intended to reopen two border points between the two countries.
